title: Enterprise throughput-to-GPU-profile alignment and SLA prioritization rubric for Dedicated
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable triage and prioritization rubric to map enterprise Dedicated requests to recommended reserved throughput envelopes, target SLAs, and GPU-class recommendations. This ticket produces: 1) a scoring model to prioritize intake, 2) a short runbook for negotiating SLA commitments with customers, 3) a guidance matrix mapping workload archetypes to GPU families and burst/scale policies, and 4) clear handoff artifacts for Sales/Customer Success and Eng on accepted requests.

Background: Over the last 9 months we've seen variability in how sales and CS surface Dedicated requests: some customers ask for blanket GPU counts, others specify token/sec targets, and a few request fixed latency SLOs without describing workload shape. Engineering needs a consistent set of inputs to size reserved pools and propose scaling rules (autoscale thresholds, burst windows, preemption tolerance). Without a triage layer we either over-provision (high cost) or under-deliver (missed SLAs).

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-offer for standard enterprise Dedicated proposals to <7 business days.
- Surface clear defaults (reserved throughput, GPU family, burst policy) for 80% of intake without deep ENG investigation.
- Provide a negotiation playbook for non-standard requests that includes acceptable SLA trade-offs and cost delta estimates.
- Produce artifacts (scorecard CSV, matrix doc, negotiation template) for cross-functional use.

Deliverables:
- Prioritization scorecard (CSV) with weighted signals: production-readiness (30%), revenue ARR impact (25%), SLA criticality (latency % of requests) (20%), engineering complexity (15%), strategic fit/partnership (10%).
- GPU Profile Matrix: recommended GPU families (A100-40G, A100-80G, H100, L4) mapped to workload archetypes (short-chat, long-context generation, high-throughput tokenization/embedding) and guidance on quantization/kv-cache expectations.
- SLA Negotiation Runbook: templated email / terms that explain SLO bands (gold/silver/bronze), typical reserved throughput vs observed p99 token latency, and cost multiplier table for dedicated vs hosted.
- Autoscaling policy defaults: min/max GPU counts, burst window (1–10m), cold-start mitigation practices, and fallback routing to compatible model variants.

Acceptance criteria:
- PMs and two Sales reps can produce an initial committed offer for a sample intake in <7 days using the scorecard and matrix.
- ENG accepts GPU profile guidance as implementable and identifies any non-trivial blockers.
- CS can present the negotiation runbook to at least two pilot customers and capture feedback.

Scope and constraints:
- This ticket focuses only on policy and playbook (non-bug). Implementation of autoscaling engines or billing changes are separate ENG tasks.
- Recommendations must respect existing capacity constraints and reserved capacity SKU nomenclature.

Stakeholders:
- PM (owner): Asha Patel
- Engineering lead (runtime/scaling): Marco Li
- Sales lead: Priya Narayanan
- CS lead: Jonah Kim
- Legal (term language advisory): Mei Chen

Risk/trade-offs:
- Conservative sizing reduces SLA incidents but increases cost to customers (risk to win rate).
- Aggressive burst policies save cost but may violate strict latency SLAs under tail workloads.
- Recommending higher-end GPUs (H100) reduces footprint but increases unit cost; must be justified by model latency/sequence needs.

Next steps:
1) Run analysis on last 12 months of dedicated intake to populate baseline distributions for requested throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency targets, and typical model families. (ENG-45012 dependency)
2) Draft initial scorecard and matrix and circulate to stakeholders.
3) Pilot with two inbound enterprise requests and iterate.
4) Finalize runbook and add to Redwood Console sales/CS playbook library.
